newsitem.title: USA: Sergeant at Aberdeen base convicted on sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Sergeant at Aberdeen base convicted on sex charges.

text.p: A military jury Thursday convicted Army Staff Sgt. Vernell Robinson Jr. on 19 counts of sexual misconduct and other offences at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground.

The jury found Robinson guilty of sodomy, indecent assault, communicating a threat, obstruction of justice, violating orders, wrongful communication and solicitation of an offence, said Ed Starnes, a spokesman for the base's Ordnance Centre and School.
The jury acquitted Robinson of one charge of interfering with U.S. mail.
A sentencing hearing will begin Friday. Robinson faced a maximum penalty of more than 60 years confinement plus a dishonourable discharge and forefiture of pay, Starnes said.
On Tuesday, before Robinson's trial begain, prosecutors dropped one count each of rape, forcible sodomy and extortion.
Robinson served as a drill instructor at the Ordnance Centre and School.
He was one of 12 soldiers at the school charged in an investigation into sexual harassment of trainees, which led to an Army-wide probe.
